b: GUILDFORD, U.K. — Raccoon Media Group, in partnership with Messe München, announced a major initiative and investment that will result in a suite of new and renewed events in 2027: a flagship ISPO Sports Week in Amsterdam and regional editions in Asia, the Middle East and the U.S.
Each regional edition will be a week-long program. Attendees and exhibitors will be able to participate not only in a B2B trade show but also in consumer events and brand experiences.

A more than $3 million investment will include more than $1 million to organize a global hosted buyer program, more than $1 million going toward a “world-class” content program, and more than $1 million to support nonprofit organizations that protect the natural environments where people play.

“Trade shows have traditionally been built around bringing buyers and sellers together, and that remains incredibly important. But the way industries operate has changed, and exhibitions need to evolve with them,” Mike Seaman, Group CEO at Raccoon Media Group, said. “In sport, clubs, athletes, creators and grassroots communities now play a significant role in shaping consumer demand, influencing purchasing decisions and driving innovation. It makes sense that they should be part of the conversation.”
ISPO Sports Week is the response to that shift.

“We’re taking the strength of a globally recognized trade show and building a much broader ecosystem around it, connecting the business of sport with the people who participate in it,” Seaman added. “That means bringing together manufacturers, brands, retailers and industry leaders alongside the communities that ultimately drive the industry forward.”

First up is ISPO Beijing, which is set for Jan. 7-10 at the China National Convention Center. The show will be organized into two halls, with a Brand Showcase on Jan. 8-10 and Sourcing Asia on Jan. 7-9.
ISPO Shanghai will follow on July 1-4 at the Shanghai New International Expo Center and adopt the same layout, with a Brand Showcase July 2-4 and Sourcing Asia July 1-3.

ISPO Sports Week Middle East will feature ISPO Source & Discover on Sept. 22-23 at the Dubai Exhibition Centre and Expo City Dubai, followed by three events on Sept. 25-26: PadelXpo Dubai, which will bring together players, fans, brands and the wider padel industry, The Run Show and OutdoorXpo Dubai, which will have eight dedicated sections covering climbing, hiking, trail running, camping and outdoor living, adventure travel, watersports, cycling and family activities.
The flagship event, ISPO — which has made its home in Munich for more than 50 years — is evolving into ISPO Sports Week Europe and moving to RAI Amsterdam.

It will kick off with the launch of PadelXpo Amsterdam and OutdoorXpo Amsterdam on Oct. 30-31, followed by the Leaders Summit on Nov. 2, then ISPO and The International Running Expo Amsterdam on Nov. 3-4.
The location and dates for the U.S. event have not been announced.
Seaman believes that this new lineup reflects where the exhibition industry is heading.

“The show floor will always have a vital role, but the opportunity is to extend its reach through events, experiences and activations that engage different audiences in different ways,” Seaman explained. “It’s about creating more opportunities for businesses to connect, while making the whole experience more relevant, accessible and valuable to the wider industry.”
